newsitem.title: USA: US rail intermodal up strongly from year ago - AAR.
newsitem.headline: US rail intermodal up strongly from year ago - AAR.

text.p: U.S. rail intermodal freight continued strong in the week ended May 10 compared to the same week a year ago, the Association of American Railroads said Thursday.
Intermodal freight, which does not include carloads, rose eight percent last week to 166,684 trailers and containers from 154,314 in the year-ago week.
AAR said ton-miles also rose 0.8 percent to 26.1 billion from 25.9 billion a year ago. The ton-mile, a measure of freight transportation, is one ton of freight hauled one mile.
Carloads stood at 343,605, down 0.5 percent from 344,350 in the year-ago week.

AAR said the largest increases in carload freight included nonmetallic minerals, which rose 15.7 percent in the May 10 week to 10,341 carloads from 8,940 in the year-ago week, and in chemicals, which increased 11.7 percent to 32,361 from 28,969.
Farm products other than grain also rose 8.8 percent to 1,246 carloads last week from 1,145 a year ago, while petroleum products loadings increased 3.8 percent to 5,554 carloads from 5,352, it said.

But AAR said carloads of motor vehicles and equipment plunged 13.3 percent in the week to 19,618 from 22,631 a year ago, while metallic ores loadings fell 10 percent to 19,763 carloads from 21,951 last year.
Grain loadings in the week were 20,424, down 6.6 percent from 21,876 in the year-ago week. Grain mill products also fell 1.1 percent to 9,432 carloads last week from 9,537 a year ago.

In the first 19 weeks of 1997, AAR said intermodal traffic rose 6.3 percent from the same period in 1996. Ton-miles rose 2.5 percent while carloads increased 1.9 percent from the same 1996 period, it said.

AAR also said intermodal traffic on the two U.S. Canada-based railroads totaled 26,047 trailers and containers in the May 10 week, up 17.8 percent from the year-ago week, while carloads totaled 56,601, up 3.7 percent from a year ago.

Combined total volume in the United States and Canada for the first 19 weeks was 7.42 million carloads, up 1.8 percent from the same 1996 period, while intermodal traffic totaled 3.52 million trailers and containers, up 6.9 percent from last year, AAR said.
